title: Two Bodies, One Warmth
logline: Through one year in a shared household, a grandchild visibly grows and a great-grandparent visibly slows, fed and warmed by the same table, the same well, the same weather.
human_question: Is the warmth that grows a child the same warmth that wears out a grandparent?

premise.story: A year of ordinary life in a multi-generation household, following one young child and one elder side by side, told through the family's own rhythms and choices about what to share.
premise.place: A multi-generation family home in a village, where several generations share meals, chores and space.
premise.experience: Shared meals, bathing at the same well, a birthday and an illness, small daily changes that only add up when looked at across a whole year.

concept_links.why: The source states plainly that one and the same ripening warmth builds up a young body and, once growth is complete, wears an older one down. A household spanning a full life makes that single claim visible without a word being said.

Grey hair, slower movement and stiffening joints are named as only the signs of decay, not decay itself, which has been present, hidden behind growth, from the start; this household can show both the growth and the sign at once.
The elder's presence quietly carries the group's closing question of what continues once a body ends, without the film needing to show a death directly.

what_camera_could_observe: Bathing or washing at the same well or tap
The child's changing abilities: crawling, first words, first steps
The elder's changing pace: a birthday, an illness, a good day and a hard one
Evening routines that repeat, with small differences, through the year
what_must_be_real: The family's own rhythms, consent and comfort at every visit over the year. No schematic 'growth versus decay' framing imposed on real people; the family's own sense of the year, not a symbolic reading of it, must lead.

possible_arc.turn: A visible change in one or the other, good or hard, becomes impossible to ignore.
possible_arc.ending_open: Wherever the year actually leaves the family.

position_hint: closing candidate: the group's clearest, most human answer to what continues when a body ends, carried by two bodies at opposite ends of one life; a strong film to end the group before it hands off to the next stage

requirements: A multi-generation household willing to be visited repeatedly across a full year
Ongoing consent from every generation, renewed at each visit
A household where an infant or young child and an elder both live together

suggestions.name: A multi-generation household in a hill-country or Uva village
suggestions.why: Extended, multi-generation households living under one roof remain common in these regions; no specific family is identified.
suggestions.verify: A specific willing family has not been found or confirmed.

risks: The elder's decline could be exploited for pathos
Framing the child as 'growth' and the elder as 'decay' would be too schematic and must be resisted
A year-long filming commitment needs genuinely ongoing, renewable consent from every generation
drop_if: No multi-generation household willing to be visited across a full year
A family member's health or circumstances make continued filming inappropriate

connections.note: One family answers 'what remains' in the days right after a death; the other watches two bodies answer the same question across a whole year.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
